name: CI

# checkov:skip=CKV2_GHA_1: CI workflow requires write permissions for uploading coverage and SARIF results
# A bare `push:` fires on EVERY branch, and `pull_request:` then re-runs the
# same work, so a feature branch was tested twice before merge and a third time
# on `dev` afterwards -- ~165 compute-minutes per PR, 56 of them for a
# docs-only plan edit. Scoping `push` to the long-lived branches drops the
# duplicate. Nothing is lost: `pull_request` still covers every feature branch,
# and it tests the MERGE commit, which is the relevant view for a squash-merge
# workflow. The branch-head view returns on the post-merge `dev` run.
#
# `main` must stay listed -- the release sync is a fast-forward PUSH to main,
# never a PR, so this is the only trigger that runs CI there. Tags no longer
# start CI, which is deliberate: `release.yml` owns `v*` and is self-contained
# (no `workflow_run`, no dependency on any ci.yml job).
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ==========================================================================
  # WHAT ACTUALLY GATES A MERGE  (#960, decided and applied 2026-08-25)
  # ==========================================================================
  # "Blocking" has meant three separable things in this repo, and a job can
  # satisfy the first two while gating nothing:
  #
  #   1. Allowed to report red        -- not `continue-on-error`.
  #   2. Cannot report green over a failure -- no `|| echo`, no `|| true`.
  #   3. Mechanically prevents a merge     -- named in a ruleset.
  #
  # Guards were repeatedly built and described as gates on meaning (1) or (2)
  # while (3) was assumed. Before #960 exactly ONE check had property (3):
  # `quick-checks`, and only on `main`. Everything else was advisory in the
  # mechanical sense, however loudly it failed.
  #
  # Required on `refs/heads/main` (ruleset 9147592, "Protect main branch"):
  #   quick-checks · cli-smoke · Windows native console encoding ·
  #   Aggregate Coverage · Lint (quick checks) ·
  #   Test ubuntu-latest Shard 1..4/4
  #
  # ADVISORY ON PURPOSE -- these can report red, and nothing stops a merge:
  #   Test windows-2022 Shard 1/1  -- `continue-on-error: true`. It reports
  #     GREEN OVER EXIT CODE 1, so requiring it would add a check that cannot
  #     fail. Read its job LOG, never its tick, and diff the skip count too.
  #   Test macos-latest Shard 1/1  -- cross-platform signal, not a gate, and as
  #     of 2026-08-30 it no longer runs on `pull_request` at all: see the
  #     matrix comment in test-sharded. It still runs on every `dev`/`main`
  #     push, so every merge is covered -- but a PR's checks list will not
  #     contain it, which is expected and not a missing report.
  #   dashboard-smoke, tool-contract-tests, policy-gate -- deliberately not in
  #     the maintainer's chosen set. policy-gate is also too new: a required
  #     check that does not yet exist on main leaves every PR waiting on a
  #     report that never arrives, so it can only be added after it has run
  #     on main at least once.
  #   phase-audit -- ADVISORY, and new for the same reason as policy-gate: it
  #     does not exist on main yet. It reports red when an open issue is in no
  #     phase of the v1.1.0 fix-program plan, or when the phase:N labels have
  #     drifted from it. Promote it in Phase 9 alongside policy-gate and
  #     docker-smoke; until then it is a visible X, not a gate, and this
  #     comment says so rather than letting the job's name imply otherwise.
  #
  # `dev` carries ruleset 21702985 ("Protect dev branch"), and its rules are
  # `deletion` and `non_fast_forward` -- nothing else. It has NO REQUIRED
  # STATUS CHECKS, so a PR into `dev` -- which is every phase PR of the v1.1.0
  # fix program -- can merge over a red advisory job. That is the recorded
  # decision (gate `main`, keep `dev` fast), not an oversight. The ruleset
  # exists for a different reason: to stop `dev` being deleted, which #993
  # added after auto-delete-on-merge ate the branch three times.
  #
  # Until #1038 this block described the branch as carrying no protection at
  # all. That was true when written and false from 2026-08-27; see #993.
  #
  # If you add a job here and intend it to gate, adding it to ci.yml is HALF
  # the work. The other half is the ruleset, and nothing in this file can tell
  # you whether that happened. Check the one that governs the branch you mean:
  #   main -> `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/rulesets/9147592`
  #   dev  -> `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/rulesets/21702985`
  # ==========================================================================

  # Fast validation checks (2-3 minutes)
  quick-checks:
    name: quick-checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        # Kept alongside the setup-uv step below: several steps in this job
        # (yamllint, the SARIF validator) pip-install standalone tools and run
        # before the project venv exists, so they need a system interpreter.
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate GitHub workflows (actionlint)
        uses: reviewdog/action-actionlint@v1.73.4
        with:
          actionlint_flags: -color
          level: error
          fail_level: error

      - name: Validate YAML files (yamllint)
        run: |
          pip install yamllint
          yamllint -c .yamllint.yaml .

      - name: Lint Dockerfile.fast
        uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3.5.0
        with:
          dockerfile: Dockerfile.fast
          failure-threshold: warning

      - name: Lint Dockerfile.slim
        uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3.5.0
        with:
          dockerfile: Dockerfile.slim
          failure-threshold: warning

      - name: Lint Dockerfile.balanced
        uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3.5.0
        with:
          dockerfile: Dockerfile.balanced
          failure-threshold: warning

      - name: Lint Dockerfile.deep
        uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3.5.0
        with:
          dockerfile: Dockerfile.deep
          failure-threshold: warning

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Verify uv.lock is up to date
        # Semantic check: "is uv.lock consistent with pyproject.toml?" This runs
        # UNCONDITIONALLY, unlike the deps-compile byte-diff gate it replaces.
        # That gate had to be scoped to non-Dependabot pull_request events because
        # Dependabot's pip resolver emitted a structurally different file than
        # `uv pip compile` -- so it could not be trusted on push or on bot PRs,
        # and main routinely sat in a format that failed the next human PR.
        # Dependabot now regenerates uv.lock *with uv*, so bot and human PRs are
        # resolver-symmetric and pass the identical gate.
        # History: PRs #321, #323, #677, #682.
        run: uv lock --check

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        shell: bash
        # Keeps every existing bare `pytest` / `ruff` invocation working
        # unchanged. Windows runners put scripts in .venv/Scripts, POSIX in
        # .venv/bin; the conditional means a job that later gains a Windows matrix
        # entry does not silently break.
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Audit Python dependencies for vulnerabilities
        # Ignored advisories and their reasoning live in the script -- one place,
        # two callers (this job and the pip-audit pre-commit hook).
        run: |
          pip install pip-audit
          bash scripts/dev/audit_deps.sh

      - name: "Guardrails: forbid tracked venv/artifacts"
        run: bash scripts/dev/guardrails_check.sh

      - name: "Secrets scan (TruffleHog)"
        run: |
          # Pinned install (versions.yaml). The upstream install.sh calls
          # GitHub's API to discover the "latest" tag and has flaked in CI
          # ("unable to find ''" errors). See PR #350 + release.rules.md
          # "CI install hardening" entry. Mirror of the Dockerfile.deep
          # download pattern (--fail + retry + integrity check). Short
          # local var `v` keeps the URL line within yamllint's 140-char limit.
          v="3.94.3"  # trufflehog version per versions.yaml
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 600 \
            "https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/releases/download/v${v}/trufflehog_${v}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
            -o /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz
          gzip -t /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz
          tar -xzf /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin trufflehog
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/trufflehog
          trufflehog filesystem . --json --exclude-paths .trufflehog-exclude.txt --only-verified > trufflehog-results.json || true
          # -c, not -r: trufflehog emits NDJSON, and `jq -r` pretty-prints each
          # matching object across ~40 lines, so `wc -l` counted *lines* rather
          # than secrets. Measured: 147 findings reported as "6090 verified
          # secrets". The pass/fail logic was right; only the number was, and a
          # 40x-inflated count reads like a breach during triage.
          VERIFIED=$(jq -c 'select(.Verified == true)' trufflehog-results.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
          if [ "$VERIFIED" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::Found $VERIFIED verified secrets! Review trufflehog-results.json"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: "Check import direction (core/cli layering)"
        run: python scripts/dev/check_import_direction.py

      - name: "Check documentation link freshness"
        run: python scripts/dev/check_doc_links.py

      - name: "Verify PyPI badge version matches pyproject.toml"
        run: |
          # Ensure badges auto-update correctly after releases
          # Detects version mismatches between local and PyPI
          bash scripts/dev/verify_badges.sh

      - name: "Lint (markdownlint, mypy, ruff)"
        run: |
          # mypy/ruff come from the uv-synced venv already on PATH.
          #
          # These three ended in `|| echo "...(non-blocking preview)"` until #960.
          # A pipeline ending in `|| echo` always exits 0, so this step -- inside
          # the ONE job branch protection actually requires -- ran three linters
          # and reported green no matter what they found. Same always-zero shape
          # as chunk 21's `if ! cmd; then rc=$?`.
          #
          # Cost of unswallowing was MEASURED first (2026-08-25), not guessed:
          #   markdownlint  0 errors on tracked files. The 3692 seen locally are
          #                 all under gitignored dirs (graphify-out/, dev-only/,
          #                 .serena/, .claude/ HANDOFFs) that a CI checkout has
          #                 no copy of, plus scripts/dashboard/node_modules --
          #                 and this job runs no `npm ci`, so that is absent too.
          #   mypy          4 errors in 1 file (scripts/dev/mcp_smoke.py), fixed
          #                 in this same PR by narrowing an MCP content union.
          #   ruff          clean, and separately blocking in lint-quick.
          #
          # `|| rc=1` assigns a literal, so all three always run and one CI round
          # trip reports every problem. Do NOT rewrite this as `if ! cmd; then
          # rc=$?` -- that reads the status of the negation, which is always 0.
          #
          # DO NOT re-add `|| echo`. A gate that runs, fails and is ignored is
          # the worst state of the three, because it looks fixed.
          rc=0

          echo "::group::Markdownlint"
          # Exclusions live in .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc "ignores" -- one source
          # of truth, so this command behaves identically on a developer box.
          npx markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md" || rc=1
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::Mypy (scripts only)"
          mypy scripts/ || rc=1
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::Ruff"
          ruff check scripts/ tests/ || rc=1
          echo "::endgroup::"

          if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::Lint failures above. The full hook suite runs nightly (scheduled.yml lint-full)."
          fi
          exit "$rc"

      - name: Validate SARIF schema
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Validating SARIF schema compliance..."

          # Install required packages for SARIF validation
          pip install jsonschema requests

          # Create and validate a minimal test SARIF file using Python
          python3 -c "
          import json, jsonschema, requests, sys, os

          # Create minimal valid SARIF 2.1.0 test file
          sarif_data = {
              '\$schema': 'https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json',
              'version': '2.1.0',
              'runs': [
                  {
                      'tool': {
                          'driver': {
                              'name': 'jmo-security-test',
                              'version': '0.8.0',
                              'informationUri': 'https://github.com/jimmy058910/jmo-security-repo'
                          }
                      },
                      'results': []
                  }
              ]
          }

          try:
              # Download SARIF 2.1.0 schema from SchemaStore (stable mirror of the
              # canonical OASIS sarif-spec schema). The old microsoft/sarif-sdk raw
              # URL was removed upstream and now 404s, which broke this gate on
              # every PR and on push to main.
              sarif_schema_url = 'https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json'
              print(f'Downloading SARIF 2.1.0 schema from SchemaStore: {sarif_schema_url}')

              response = requests.get(sarif_schema_url, timeout=30)
              response.raise_for_status()

              schema = response.json()
              print('✅ SARIF schema downloaded and parsed successfully')

              # Validate the test SARIF file
              jsonschema.validate(sarif_data, schema)
              print('✅ SARIF schema validation passed')
              print('✅ SARIF reporter can generate valid SARIF 2.1.0 files')

          except requests.RequestException as e:
              print(f'❌ Failed to download SARIF schema: {e}')
              sys.exit(1)
          except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
              print(f'❌ Failed to parse SARIF schema JSON: {e}')
              sys.exit(1)
          except Exception as e:
              print(f'❌ SARIF validation failed: {e}')
              sys.exit(1)
          "

  # Sharded test execution across all platforms
  # Ubuntu: 4 parallel shards with coverage (primary CI target)
  # macOS/Windows: single shard each, no coverage (cross-platform validation)
  test-sharded:
    name: Test ${{ matrix.os }} Shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ matrix.total-shards }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # macOS is ADVISORY -- see the gating comment at the top of this file. It
      # is not one of the nine checks the `main` ruleset requires, yet it is
      # ~11 of this workflow's ~55 compute-minutes and carries a 10x multiplier
      # wherever Actions is billed. So it runs on `dev`/`main` pushes -- which
      # means on every merge -- and on workflow_dispatch, but not on each PR
      # revision. Ubuntu and Windows are unchanged on both events.
      #
      # This must be built as a single `include:` expression. `exclude:` cannot
      # express it: exclude is applied BEFORE include, so it never removes an
      # entry that include added -- and every entry here comes from include.
      matrix:
        include: >-
          ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request'
          && '[{"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":1,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":2,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":3,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":4,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"windows-2022","shard":1,"total-shards":1}]'
          || '[{"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":1,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":2,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":3,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"ubuntu-latest","shard":4,"total-shards":4},
          {"os":"macos-latest","shard":1,"total-shards":1},
          {"os":"windows-2022","shard":1,"total-shards":1}]') }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dependencies
        # Replaces two pip installs wrapped in 3-attempt retry loops. uv sync is
        # a single atomic operation with its own network retries, and it installs
        # the project editable as well, so the separate `pip install -e .` goes away.
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        shell: bash
        # This matrix spans ubuntu, macOS and Windows. Windows needs a
        # WINDOWS-style path: Git Bash resolves POSIX entries like
        # /d/a/repo/.venv/Scripts itself, so `python -m pytest` runs fine, but the
        # Python process inherits the raw PATH string and shutil.which() on Windows
        # cannot interpret a POSIX path -- so every external tool lookup (bandit,
        # semgrep, trivy...) silently returns None and tool-discovery tests fail
        # while everything else passes. cygpath -w fixes it; the POSIX branch only
        # ever runs on Linux/macOS.
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Run sharded tests with coverage (Ubuntu)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        env:
          CI: "true"
          PYTHONUTF8: "1"
          JMO_THREADS: "2"
        run: |
          python -m pytest -q \
            --disable-warnings \

  # The only job that runs as an ordinary Windows user does.
  #
  # Every other test step above sets PYTHONUTF8: "1", which enables Python UTF-8
  # Mode and overrides the locale codec for open(), read_text() AND stdio. On
  # Linux/macOS that changes nothing (already UTF-8); on Windows it substitutes
  # an environment nobody actually has, so those shards structurally cannot
  # observe this bug class. That is how 40 failures and 22 errors sat on main
  # under a green tick while `jmo trends explain score` exited 1 for every
  # Windows user.
  #
  # Everything except the console codec is identical to the windows-2022 shard,
  # so a failure here is attributable to the codec and nothing else.
  #
  # DO NOT add PYTHONUTF8 here, and DO NOT add continue-on-error. Either one
  # makes this job decorative. See
  # .claude/rules/testing.cross-platform.rules.md "Console Encoding (Windows)".
  windows-native-encoding:
    name: Windows native console encoding
    runs-on: windows-2022
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        # cygpath -w is mandatory: shutil.which() on Windows cannot read a POSIX
        # PATH entry, so tool discovery silently returns None. See the same step
        # in test-sharded for the full explanation.
        run: |
          cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Configure Windows temp directory for faster I/O
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "D:\Temp" | Out-Null
          "TEMP=D:\Temp" | Out-File -Append $env:GITHUB_ENV
          "TMP=D:\Temp" | Out-File -Append $env:GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Report the console codec this job actually got
        # Proves the job is testing what it claims to. If this ever prints utf-8,
        # something upstream (a runner image change, an inherited env var) has
        # silently neutralised the job.
        run: |
          python -c "import sys, locale; print(
            'stdout:', sys.stdout.encoding,
            '| preferred:', locale.getpreferredencoding(False),
            '| utf8_mode:', sys.flags.utf8_mode)"

      - name: Assert the suite still collects
        # `0 tests collected` exits 0, and a conftest that quietly stops
        # collecting a package (mcp 2.0 hid 235 tests behind a green tick)
        # exits 0 too. Only a count floor catches that. Measured 7935 with this
        # filter; the floor is a deliberate tripwire -- if you legitimately
        # remove tests, lower it in the same PR and say why.
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: |
          collected=$(python -m pytest --collect-only -q \
            -m "not smoke and not requires_tools and not docker and not slow" \
            | grep -oE "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+ tests collected" | cut -d/ -f1)
          echo "collected: ${collected:-0} (floor: 7800)"
          if [ -z "$collected" ] || [ "$collected" -lt 7800 ]; then
            echo "::error::Collected ${collected:-0} tests, expected >=7800." \
              "Collection broke, or tests were removed without lowering the floor."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Assert the optional-dependency packages still collect
        # THE GLOBAL FLOOR ABOVE CANNOT CATCH WHAT ITS OWN COMMENT CITES.
        # Measured at chunk 20: 8993 collected against a floor of 7800 is 1193
        # of headroom, and tests/jmo_mcp is 295 tests -- the package the mcp 2.0
        # rename silently emptied can vanish *four times over* and the global
        # assertion still passes.
        #
        # The per-package floor is set close enough to catch a single test FILE
        # failing to collect, not just the whole tree going to zero. That means
        # the arithmetic is: floor <= collected - (smallest file - 1), so losing
        # the smallest file drops BELOW it.
        #
        # THE HEADROOM IS PART OF THE SPEC, AND THIS FLOOR MISSED ITS OWN.
        # Chunk 20 set 280 against 295 collected -- 15 of headroom against a
        # smallest file of 13, so `test_auth.py` failing to collect would have
        # left 282, and 282 > 280 passes. The floor could not catch the case
        # its comment describes. Same shape as the global floor it was added to
        # fix, one order of magnitude down. Re-measured at chunk 22.1:
        # 314 collected, smallest file still 13, so the floor is 302.
        #
        # A package gated behind an optional dependency is the case that needs
        # its own floor: the failure mode is an import probe going false, which
        # takes out the whole tree at once and exits 0. Packages that are not
        # gated fail loudly on a collection error, so they do not need an entry
        # here. Raise a floor in the same PR that adds tests -- and recompute it
        # from the smallest file, do not just add the delta.
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: |
          fail=0
          check_package() {
            pkg="$1"; floor="$2"
            # pytest prints TWO different summary lines and this must read both:
            #   "295 tests collected in 0.2s"            (nothing deselected)
            #   "260/295 tests collected (35 deselected)" (something deselected)
            # Matching only the first form means the day any test in the package
            # gains a `slow`/`docker` marker, this reads empty, reports 0, and
            # fires spuriously. Take the leading number either way -- that is
            # the SELECTED count, same as the global check's `cut -d/ -f1`.
            n=$(python -m pytest "$pkg" --collect-only -q \
              -m "not smoke and not requires_tools and not docker and not slow" \
              | grep -oE "^[0-9]+(/[0-9]+)? tests collected" \
              | sed -E 's|^([0-9]+).*|\1|')
            echo "${pkg}: ${n:-0} collected (floor: ${floor})"
            if [ -z "$n" ] || [ "$n" -lt "$floor" ]; then
              echo "::error::${pkg} collected ${n:-0} tests, expected >=${floor}." \
                "An optional-dependency probe went false, or tests were removed" \
                "without lowering the floor. Uncollected tests cannot fail."
              fail=1
            fi
          }
          check_package tests/jmo_mcp 302
          exit "$fail"

      - name: Run the full suite on a native (non-UTF-8) console
        # PYTHONUTF8 is DELIBERATELY ABSENT -- that is the entire point.
        # Flags match the windows-2022 shard exactly so the codec is the only
        # variable. Not `-m native_encoding`: the read-side class lives in
        # ordinary tests all over the suite and a marker cannot see it.
        env:
          CI: "true"
          JMO_THREADS: "2"
        run: |
          python -m pytest -q \
            --disable-warnings \
            --timeout=60 \
            -p no:xdist \
            -p no:rerunfailures \
            -m "not smoke and not requires_tools and not docker and not slow"

      - name: Windows post-test cleanup
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $procs = Get-Process -Name python,cmd,node,java -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.Id -ne $PID }
          if ($procs) {
            Write-Host "Killing $($procs.Count) orphan processes"
            $procs | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
          }

  # Aggregate coverage from all shards and upload to Codecov
  coverage-aggregate:
    name: Aggregate Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test-sharded
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write  # Needed for Codecov OIDC
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Download all coverage artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-ubuntu-latest-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Install coverage tool
        run: pip install coverage[toml]

      - name: Combine coverage reports
        run: |
          # List downloaded coverage files
          echo "📊 Coverage files from shards:"
          ls -la coverage-shard-*.xml

          # Combine XML reports using coverage.py
          # First convert XML to .coverage files, then combine
          pip install coverage[toml]

          # Create a simple Python script to merge XML coverage
          python3 << 'EOF'
          import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          import glob
          import re
          import sys

          # Helpers for branch-coverage merging (extends PR #357's line-rate fix).
          # `condition-coverage` from coverage.py is "X% (covered/total)";
          # `missing-branches` is a comma-separated list of branch targets
          # (line numbers) — OMITTED entirely when nothing is missing, never
          # emitted as an empty string. So absent attribute means "all
          # branches covered on this line in this shard".

          def parse_missing_branches(s):
              if not s:
                  return set()
              return {b.strip() for b in s.split(',') if b.strip()}

          def parse_condition_total(s):
              # Returns the `total` from "X% (covered/total)"; 0 if not parseable.
              if not s:
                  return 0
              m = re.search(r'\((\d+)/(\d+)\)', s)
              return int(m.group(2)) if m else 0

          def merge_branch_attrs(existing, incoming):
              """Update `existing` <line> in-place with the union of branch
              coverage data from `incoming`. A branch counts as covered in the
              merged output if covered in EITHER shard, equivalent to:
                  union_missing = existing_missing ∩ incoming_missing
              Total branch count is the same in both shards (same source code);
              we take max defensively in case one shard skipped the line.
              """
              if existing.get('branch') != 'true' and incoming.get('branch') != 'true':
                  return
              existing_missing = parse_missing_branches(existing.get('missing-branches', ''))
              incoming_missing = parse_missing_branches(incoming.get('missing-branches', ''))
              union_missing = existing_missing & incoming_missing  # intersection: missing in BOTH
              total = max(
                  parse_condition_total(existing.get('condition-coverage', '')),
                  parse_condition_total(incoming.get('condition-coverage', '')),
              )
              if total <= 0:
                  return
              covered = total - len(union_missing)
              pct = (covered / total) * 100
              existing.set('branch', 'true')
              existing.set('condition-coverage', f"{pct:.0f}% ({covered}/{total})")
              if union_missing:
                  # Lex sort handles coverage.py's non-numeric branch targets
                  # (e.g. "exit" when a branch leaves the function); int() sort
                  # raises ValueError on those and would silently abort the
                  # outer per-file try/except, dropping the whole shard's merge.
                  existing.set('missing-branches', ','.join(sorted(union_missing)))
              elif 'missing-branches' in existing.attrib:
                  # Fully covered after merge — drop the attribute to match
                  # coverage.py's emission convention (it omits, doesn't empty).
                  del existing.attrib['missing-branches']

          def merge_coverage_xml(files, output):
              """Merge multiple coverage XML files into one."""
              if not files:
                  print("No coverage files to merge")
                  sys.exit(1)

              # Parse first file as base
              base_tree = ET.parse(files[0])
              base_root = base_tree.getroot()
              base_packages = base_root.find('.//packages')

              if base_packages is None:
                  # Cobertura format
                  base_packages = base_root.find('packages')

              # Track merged data
              merged_files = {}

              def process_package(pkg):
                  """Extract file data from a package element.

                  Uses pkg.findall('.//class') to locate <class> elements
                  regardless of whether they're nested under <classes> (cobertura
                  default) or direct children of <package>. The previous
                  implementation tried to detect both via
                  `pkg.find('classes') or pkg.findall('class')` and a downstream
                  `hasattr(classes, '__iter__')` guard — but ElementTree's
                  Element type uses the legacy __getitem__ iteration protocol
                  (no __iter__ dunder), so the hasattr check returned False
                  whenever the cobertura <classes> wrapper was present, silently
                  skipping the entire merge. Result: coverage.xml was a copy of
                  shard-1's XML, and the threshold read shard-1's coverage in
                  isolation (~68-72%) instead of the true aggregate (~88%).
                  """
                  for cls in pkg.findall('.//class'):
                      filename = cls.get('filename')
                      if not filename:
                          continue
                      if filename not in merged_files:
                          merged_files[filename] = cls
                      else:
                          # Merge line coverage: OR the hits per line number,
                          # AND union the per-line branch coverage.
                          existing_lines = {l.get('number'): l for l in merged_files[filename].findall('.//line')}
                          for line in cls.findall('.//line'):
                              line_num = line.get('number')
                              if line_num in existing_lines:
                                  # Same line in both shards — take max hits (covered in any shard = covered)
                                  existing_hits = int(existing_lines[line_num].get('hits', 0))
                                  new_hits = int(line.get('hits', 0))
                                  existing_lines[line_num].set('hits', str(max(existing_hits, new_hits)))
                                  # Union branch coverage on the same line.
                                  merge_branch_attrs(existing_lines[line_num], line)
                              else:
                                  # Line only in the new shard — append to the merged class's <lines>
                                  lines_elem = merged_files[filename].find('lines')
                                  if lines_elem is not None:
                                      lines_elem.append(line)

              # Process all packages in base
              for pkg in base_root.findall('.//package'):
                  process_package(pkg)

              # Merge additional files
              for f in files[1:]:
                  try:
                      tree = ET.parse(f)
                      root = tree.getroot()
                      for pkg in root.findall('.//package'):
                          process_package(pkg)
                  except Exception as e:
                      print(f"Warning: Could not process {f}: {e}")

              # Recompute aggregate line-rate from merged <line> hits.
              # The merge above OR's hits across shards but the root <coverage>
              # element's line-rate/lines-valid/lines-covered attributes still
              # reflect shard-1's standalone values. Without this recomputation
              # the threshold check downstream reads shard-1's coverage in
              # isolation (~68-72%) instead of the true merged aggregate (~88%).
              # See PR #355 / CHANGELOG for the empirical investigation.
              total_lines = covered_lines = 0
              for line in base_root.findall('.//line'):
                  total_lines += 1
                  if int(line.get('hits', 0)) > 0:
                      covered_lines += 1
              if total_lines:
                  rate = covered_lines / total_lines
                  base_root.set('line-rate', f"{rate:.4f}")
                  base_root.set('lines-valid', str(total_lines))
                  base_root.set('lines-covered', str(covered_lines))
                  print(f"📊 Aggregate: {covered_lines}/{total_lines} lines covered = {rate * 100:.2f}%")

              # Recompute aggregate branch-rate from merged <line branch="true">
              # condition-coverage attributes. Each merged line has already had
              # its missing-branches set-intersected across shards by
              # merge_branch_attrs, so the per-line covered/total counts are
              # correct unions. Summing them gives the true aggregate. Without
              # this pass, branch-rate/branches-valid/branches-covered remain at
              # shard-1's standalone values (the same scope-limit that PR #357
              # left for line-rate's sibling attrs). The CI threshold check only
              # uses line-rate, so this is currently informational; if a future
              # branch-coverage threshold is added, it'll read true aggregates.
              total_branches = covered_branches = 0
              for line in base_root.findall('.//line'):
                  if line.get('branch') != 'true':
                      continue
                  cc = line.get('condition-coverage', '')
                  m = re.search(r'\((\d+)/(\d+)\)', cc)
                  if not m:
                      continue
                  covered_branches += int(m.group(1))
                  total_branches += int(m.group(2))
              if total_branches:
                  branch_rate = covered_branches / total_branches
                  base_root.set('branch-rate', f"{branch_rate:.4f}")
                  base_root.set('branches-valid', str(total_branches))
                  base_root.set('branches-covered', str(covered_branches))
                  print(f"📊 Branches: {covered_branches}/{total_branches} branches covered = {branch_rate * 100:.2f}%")

              # Write merged output
              base_tree.write(output, encoding='unicode', xml_declaration=True)
              print(f"✅ Merged {len(files)} coverage files into {output}")

          # Find and merge all shard coverage files
          coverage_files = sorted(glob.glob('coverage-shard-*.xml'))
          print(f"Found {len(coverage_files)} coverage files: {coverage_files}")
          merge_coverage_xml(coverage_files, 'coverage.xml')
          EOF

      - name: Verify coverage threshold
        run: |
          # Parse coverage.xml and check threshold
          python3 << 'EOF'
          import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          import sys

          tree = ET.parse('coverage.xml')
          root = tree.getroot()

          # Get line-rate from coverage element
          line_rate = float(root.get('line-rate', 0))
          coverage_pct = line_rate * 100

          print(f"📊 Combined coverage: {coverage_pct:.2f}%")

          # CI threshold is 85% (excludes requires_tools/docker/smoke tests).
          # The aggregate XML merge in the previous step recomputes line-rate
          # from merged <line> hits, so this reads true aggregate coverage
          # rather than shard-1's standalone value (which was the source of
          # the spurious "drop from 71.6% to 68.7%" investigated in PR #355).
          #
          # History: 70 -> 80 after measuring 86.4%, stable +/-0.1 over 5 runs.
          # 80 -> 85 under #756, after measuring 86.87% (19704/22681 lines) on
          # the last main run. At 80 the gate carried 6.87 points of slack --
          # roughly 1550 lines could have gone uncovered with CI still green,
          # which is not a floor so much as a formality.
          #
          # Headroom is part of the spec, so it is stated: 1.87 points, ~424
          # lines, against a measured run-to-run variance of +/-0.1. That is
          # ~19x the noise, which is the margin #792 did NOT have -- its 500MB
          # RSS cap sat about 1% above a quantity that moved 111MB on machine
          # state alone, so it tripped on noise instead of on regressions.
          # If this gate starts flapping, re-measure the variance before
          # lowering the floor; a flapping gate means the assumption above is
          # wrong, not that the number is too high.
          #
          # `--cov-fail-under` remains unset repo-wide: this is the only
          # enforced coverage floor in the project. Cite it as
          # "coverage-aggregate's Verify coverage threshold step", never by
          # line number -- the number has moved three times (734, 788, 816).
          if coverage_pct < 85:
              print(f"❌ Coverage {coverage_pct:.2f}% is below 85% CI threshold")
              sys.exit(1)
          else:
              print(f"✅ Coverage {coverage_pct:.2f}% meets 85% CI threshold")
          EOF

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          verbose: true


  # Quick lint checks for PRs - formatters in check-only mode
  lint-quick:
    name: Lint (quick checks)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dev dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        shell: bash
        # pre-commit, ruff and shfmt are invoked bare in later steps.
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Cache pre-commit environments
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-precommit-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-precommit-

      - name: Run pre-commit (quick checks)
        env:
          # Don't set PRE_COMMIT_HOME: YAML env: passes ~ literally (no shell expansion),
          # so `~/.cache/pre-commit` becomes a literal directory under $PWD which defeats
          # the cache action and litters the repo root. Pre-commit's default
          # ($HOME/.cache/pre-commit on Linux) matches the cache action's path.
          # Skip the ruff hooks that have a dedicated check-only step below
          # (ruff format --check, ruff check). shfmt was in this list until #960 --
          # see the shfmt hook invocation below for why it had to come out.
          SKIP: ruff,ruff-format,bandit,mypy
        run: |
          # Run core linting hooks
          pre-commit run --all-files trailing-whitespace
          pre-commit run --all-files end-of-file-fixer
          pre-commit run --all-files check-yaml
          pre-commit run --all-files check-json
          pre-commit run --all-files check-toml
          pre-commit run --all-files mixed-line-ending
          pre-commit run --all-files detect-private-key
          pre-commit run --all-files check-added-large-files
          # CLAUDE.md and .gitignore both promise this "fails CI and pre-commit".
          # Until it ran here, only the nightly all-hooks job enforced it, so a
          # broken documentation link could merge and sit until the next night.
          pre-commit run --all-files doc-links
          # shfmt via its pinned hook (v3.13.1-1), NOT a bare binary. The step
          # this replaces was `shfmt -d ... 2>/dev/null || true`, and shfmt is
          # installed by nothing in this job: it is absent from pyproject.toml
          # and uv.lock, and exists only as the pre-commit hook below. So the
          # bare call hit command-not-found, `2>/dev/null` ate the message and
          # `|| true` ate exit 127 -- the step reported success having checked
          # nothing, for its entire life. Measured under #960.
          #
          # The hook also covers more: `types: [shell]` is every shell file in
          # the repo, where the old globs were scripts/dev/*.sh + scripts/core/*.sh.
          # It writes, so a formatting drift surfaces as "files were modified by
          # this hook" and fails the run -- which is the check we wanted.
          pre-commit run --all-files shfmt

      - name: Check Python formatting (ruff format --check)
        run: |
          ruff format --check scripts/ tests/

      - name: Check Python linting (ruff check)
        run: |
          ruff check scripts/ tests/

  # Owns the two halves of the dashboard contract that the test shards cannot.
  #
  #   1. The wheel actually carries the bundle. Before #862 it did not: a wheel
  #      built from a clean checkout held 196 entries and 0 under
  #      scripts/dashboard/, because `dist/` was covered by a blanket
  #      `.gitignore` rule and `packages.find` collects Python packages only.
  #      A pip-installed `jmo report` produced a 2,468-byte static page every
  #      time while the README advertised a React dashboard. The shards assert
  #      the bundle is present in the TREE; only building a wheel proves it is
  #      in the DISTRIBUTION, so that check is here and is unconditional.
  #
  #   2. The tracked bundle still matches its sources. That needs Node, so it
  #      cannot live in the shards. It replaces the mtime check that used to be
  #      in html_reporter: with `dist/` tracked, git checkout order made every
  #      build input newer than the bundle, so that check reported "stale" on
  #      every fresh clone (measured: 17.3 ms of spread, all 7 inputs newer).
  #
  # The paths filter is deliberately wider than `scripts/dashboard/**`.
  # `html_reporter.py` depends on the build contract (it string-replaces a
  # placeholder the bundle must contain) and `pyproject.toml` / `.gitignore` /
  # `.gitattributes` are what put the bundle in the wheel intact -- a change to
  # any of them can break shipping without touching a dashboard source file.
  #
  # NOTE: this job is advisory -- it is not in ruleset 9147592's required set.
  # Promoting it belongs with policy-gate and phase-audit in Phase 9.
  dashboard-smoke:
    name: dashboard-smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Detect dashboard changes
        id: changes
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            dashboard:
              - 'scripts/dashboard/**'
              - 'scripts/core/reporters/html_reporter.py'
              - 'pyproject.toml'
              - '.gitignore'
              - '.gitattributes'

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      # Unconditional: the distribution check.
      #
      # setuptools keeps two caches `uv build` never invalidates, and they break
      # this check in OPPOSITE directions, so both are removed first. A fresh
      # runner has neither -- this is what keeps the step honest when someone
      # runs it locally, where it was measurably vacuous without them:
      #   build/lib/             never pruned, so the wheel ships files the tree
      #                          no longer has (measured: scripts/cli/scan_jobs/
      #                          base_scanner.py, deleted in 841cf7d2, in a
      #                          wheel built months later from a clean worktree)
      #   *.egg-info/SOURCES.txt re-read under include-package-data, so the
      #                          wheel ships files whose package-data
      #                          declaration was deleted -- this check passed
      #                          against a pyproject.toml with no
      #                          [tool.setuptools.package-data] at all
      - name: Verify the wheel carries the built dashboard
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rm -rf build dist ./*.egg-info
          uv build --wheel --out-dir dist-check
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib
          import pathlib
          import sys
          import zipfile

          wheel = next(pathlib.Path("dist-check").glob("*.whl"))
          member = "scripts/dashboard/dist/index.html"
          with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as zf:
              names = zf.namelist()
              print(f"{wheel.name}: {len(names)} entries")
              if member not in names:
                  under = [n for n in names if n.startswith("scripts/dashboard/")]
                  print(f"::error::{member} is not in the wheel "
                        f"({len(under)} entries under scripts/dashboard/). "
                        "A pip-installed jmo would render the static fallback. "
                        "Check [tool.setuptools.package-data] in pyproject.toml "
                        "and the dist/ negations in .gitignore.")
                  sys.exit(1)
              packaged = zf.read(member)

          tracked = pathlib.Path(member).read_bytes()
          print(f"packaged {len(packaged)} B  sha256={hashlib.sha256(packaged).hexdigest()}")
          print(f"tracked  {len(tracked)} B  sha256={hashlib.sha256(tracked).hexdigest()}")
          if packaged != tracked:
              print("::error::the wheel's dashboard differs from the tracked one")
              sys.exit(1)
          print("OK: the wheel ships the tracked dashboard bundle verbatim")
          PY

      - name: Set up Node.js 22
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard == 'true'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: scripts/dashboard/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dashboard dependencies
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard == 'true'
        working-directory: scripts/dashboard
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build dashboard (tsc && vite build)
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard == 'true'
        working-directory: scripts/dashboard
        run: npm run build

      # The freshness gate. `npm run build` writes over the tracked file, so
      # git itself is the comparison: if the rebuild reproduces what is
      # committed there is no diff. Measured locally before this existed: two
      # consecutive builds and one from three days earlier all produced
      # sha256 664766e5..., so the build is byte-reproducible on one machine.
      # Whether Linux reproduces a Windows build is what this step measures for
      # the first time -- if it turns out not to, the honest fix is a property
      # comparison here, not deleting the gate.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches a fresh build
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if git diff --quiet -- scripts/dashboard/dist/index.html; then
            echo "OK: the committed bundle reproduces byte for byte"
            exit 0
          fi
          {
            echo "::error::scripts/dashboard/dist/index.html is out of date."
            echo "committed: $(git show HEAD:scripts/dashboard/dist/index.html | sha256sum)"
            echo "rebuilt:   $(sha256sum < scripts/dashboard/dist/index.html)"
            echo "Run 'npm run build' in scripts/dashboard/ and commit the result."
          }
          exit 1

      - name: Test dashboard (jest)
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard == 'true'
        working-directory: scripts/dashboard
        run: npm test

      - name: Skip note (no dashboard source changes)
        if: steps.changes.outputs.dashboard != 'true'
        run: echo "No dashboard-relevant changes; the wheel check above still ran."

  # The only job that runs `jmo` the way a user does.
  #
  # Before this existed, a PR ran 8,995 tests and invoked ZERO jmo subcommands.
  # The only two anywhere were `jmo --help` in scheduled.yml -- guarded with
  # `|| echo`, so it cannot fail -- and `jmo validate` in the TAG-ONLY release
  # workflow. Every test in the suite imports the functions and calls them as
  # plain Python, which is why the v1.1.0 audit kept finding commands that were
  # advertised and inert: `jmo mcp-server --api-key` set an environment
  # variable no code read for its entire life (#716), and `jmo verify` reported
  # success having compared zero digests, with CI green throughout.
  #
  # DO NOT add continue-on-error. A gate that cannot block is a gate that
  # reports the thing it was built to catch as fine -- see the windows-2022
  # shard above, which is continue-on-error and shows green over exit code 1.
  #
  # Both scripts run identically on a developer's machine, which is how their
  # negative controls are exercised: break tool registration, or
  # `_verify_subject_digest`, and watch them go red. #948, #954.
  cli-smoke:
    name: cli-smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        # `uv sync` creates .venv but does not activate it, and setup-uv leaves
        # its own 3.12 on PATH. Without this, `python` below is the wrong
        # interpreter and the mcp import fails for a reason that looks like a
        # missing dependency. GITHUB_PATH entries are prepended.
        run: echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Report the interpreter this job actually got
        # Proves the step above worked, in the same spirit as
        # windows-native-encoding's codec probe. Both smoke scripts run through
        # `python`, so a silent fallback to the system interpreter would make
        # them fail on an ImportError that reads as a broken dependency.
        run: |
          python -c "import sys, mcp; print('python:', sys.executable); \
            print('mcp:', mcp.__file__)"
          case "$(python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)')" in
            "$PWD/.venv/"*) echo "OK: project venv" ;;
            *) echo "::error::python is not the project venv"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - name: MCP server -- start it, speak stdio, list and call its tools
        # Fails if the server cannot start (exit 2), if the five tools are not
        # registered, if an undocumented sixth appears, if the finding://
        # resource template is missing, or if a real call over the wire errors.
        # No network, no secrets. ~20s.
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: python scripts/dev/mcp_smoke.py

      - name: attest/verify -- prove the tamper checks still fail
        # Steps 3-5 are the point. Step 2 alone passes against a verifier that
        # returns 0 unconditionally, which is close to what shipped.
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: python scripts/dev/attest_smoke.py

  # The only job that evaluates real Rego policies. #922.
  #
  # Before this existed, NO workflow installed `opa` -- `grep -rn '\bopa\b'
  # .github/workflows/` returned only "propagation" and "opaque" -- so all 20
  # behavioural policy tests skipped on every runner, including the 15 that were
  # chunk 16's acceptance criterion for the entire policy surface. Chunk 16 found
  # two SHIPPED policies (zero-secrets, hipaa-compliance) that could not fire on
  # any input and answered PASS for everything. CI could not have caught either,
  # and until now still could not.
  #
  # Why this ALWAYS runs, rather than being folded in or path-gated:
  #   - #922 proposed adding opa to tool-contract-tests. Measured: that job is
  #     paths-filtered to versions.yaml / Dockerfile.* / test_tool_contracts.py,
  #     so editing a policy would not trigger it. The gate would sit dark over
  #     exactly the changes it exists to catch.
  #   - Path-gating on policies/** would be wrong for a second reason: these
  #     tests are also sensitive to ADAPTER changes. test_policy_field_contract.py
  #     exists precisely because a policy can dereference a field no adapter
  #     produces, and that break arrives via an adapter edit.
  # Cost is ~2 min: one pinned ~100MB static binary and 20 tests.
  #
  # DO NOT add continue-on-error, and do not let the opa install fail softly --
  # see the guard step, which exists because a skipped test and a passing test
  # are indistinguishable in a summary line.
  policy-gate:
    name: policy-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Install opa
        env:
          # Pinned to versions.yaml (opa.version). Update both together.
          OPA_VERSION: "1.20.1"
        run: |
          # Hardened per release.rules.md "CI install hardening": --fail so an
          # HTML error page is never mistaken for a binary, retries for the CDN
          # flakes that have broken other installs here, bounded timeouts. This
          # is a bare static binary, so there is no archive to `gzip -t`; the
          # `opa version` call below is the integrity check.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors \
            --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 600 \
            "https://github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/releases/download/v${OPA_VERSION}/opa_linux_amd64_static" \
            -o /usr/local/bin/opa
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/opa
          opa version

      - name: "Guard: opa must resolve, or the tests below skip silently"
        # Without this, a failed or mislocated install makes every policy test
        # SKIP -- and pytest reports skips as success, so the job would go green
        # having evaluated no policy at all. That is the precise failure this job
        # was created to end, so it must not be reproducible inside it.
        #
        # Asks the question the way the PRODUCT asks it: find_tool, not
        # shutil.which. They disagree -- find_tool also searches ~/.jmo/bin and
        # the interpreter's Scripts dir, which is how `jmo tools install opa`
        # places it. Both test files gate on find_tool, so this one check covers
        # them both.
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import sys

          from scripts.core.tool_utils import find_tool

          resolved = find_tool("opa")
          if resolved is None:
              print(
                  "::error::opa did not resolve via find_tool(). The policy tests "
                  "would SKIP and this job would report green having tested nothing."
              )
              sys.exit(1)
          print(f"opa resolves to: {resolved}")
          PY

      - name: Run real-policy tests
        # -rs prints skip reasons, so if anything skips despite the guard above
        # the log says why instead of hiding it in a count.
        run: |
          pytest tests/integration/test_builtin_policy_decisions.py \
                 tests/performance/test_policy_performance.py \
                 -q -rs --timeout=300

  # PR-time Docker gate. #962.
  #
  # The 60 tests in tests/e2e/test_docker_workflows.py were executed by NOTHING:
  # `grep -rn 'test_docker_workflows\|-m docker' .github/workflows/` returned
  # nothing, and every marker filter in ci.yml and scheduled.yml carries
  # `not docker`. Chunk 21 ran them by hand once and immediately found defects
  # that had never been evaluated -- an image-size assertion failing on every
  # published variant (#961), and 26 call sites collapsing "no daemon", "tag
  # missing", "not logged in" and "pull timed out" into one identical SKIP.
  #
  # Why PATH-GATED rather than on every PR. With JMO_DOCKER_REGISTRY unset these
  # tests audit the LAST RELEASED image, and images rebuild only on a `v*` tag
  # push. Between tags the subject under test is therefore a CONSTANT: running
  # them on every PR re-measures an unchanging artifact for real CI minutes and
  # no new information. The answer can only move when a Dockerfile, the test
  # file, or the tool registry driving the expected-tool counts changes.
  #
  # And why it BUILDS rather than pulls: a Dockerfile change does not alter what
  # is published, so testing the published image would not test the change. The
  # fast variant is used because it is the cheapest build that still exercises
  # the whole path; the full four-variant sweep runs weekly in scheduled.yml
  # against the published images, which is the other half of this gate.
  #
  # Scope is logged rather than left implicit -- `-k fast` selects 13 of 60, and
  # a job that quietly tests a fifth of what its name suggests is its own kind
  # of lie.
  docker-smoke:
    name: docker-smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Detect Docker-affecting changes
        id: changes
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            docker:
              - 'Dockerfile.*'
              - 'tests/e2e/test_docker_workflows.py'
              - 'scripts/core/tool_registry.py'

      - name: Set up uv
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Build the fast variant from THIS PR
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        run: docker build -t jmo-security-pr:fast -f Dockerfile.fast .

      - name: "Guard: the image must exist, or every test below skips"
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        # ensure_image() pulls when an image is absent locally, and
        # `jmo-security-pr` is not a registry, so a silently-failed build would
        # turn into a pull failure rather than a clear "the build broke". Assert
        # the artifact first so the failure names its own cause.
        run: |
          docker image inspect jmo-security-pr:fast --format 'built {{.Id}}'

      - name: Run the fast-variant Docker tests
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker == 'true'
        env:
          # Point the suite at the image built above, NOT the published one --
          # otherwise this job would test an artifact the PR cannot affect.
          JMO_DOCKER_REGISTRY: jmo-security-pr
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Running the fast-variant subset (13 of 60 tests)."
          echo "::notice::The other 47 target slim/balanced/deep, which this job"
          echo "::notice::does not build. They run weekly in scheduled.yml"
          echo "::notice::against the published images."
          pytest tests/e2e/test_docker_workflows.py -k fast -m docker -q -rs --timeout=900

      - name: Skip note (no Docker-affecting changes)
        if: steps.changes.outputs.docker != 'true'
        run: |
          echo "No Dockerfile.*, test_docker_workflows.py or tool_registry.py changes."
          echo "These tests audit the last RELEASED image, which only a v* tag rebuilds,"
          echo "so nothing in this PR can change their answer. Full sweep runs weekly."

  # Tool-output contract tests for PRs that bump tool versions.
  #
  # This job is a required status check for PRs labeled dependencies+automated
  # (see docs/RELEASE.md -> "Tool-Version Auto-Merge"). It must ALWAYS run
  # (so the required-check name stays stable for branch protection) but only
  # does real work when versions.yaml or Dockerfile.* changed — other PRs get
  # a trivial pass via the paths-filter step.
  #
  # Both the job key AND `name:` are pinned to `tool-contract-tests` so branch
  # protection can match the exact string without surprises.
  tool-contract-tests:
    name: tool-contract-tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Detect version-affecting changes
        id: changes
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            versions:
              - 'versions.yaml'
              - 'Dockerfile.*'
              - 'tests/integration/test_tool_contracts.py'

      - name: Set up uv
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions == 'true'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          version: "0.11.15"  # pinned: single uv version across all sites (PR #488)
          python-version: '3.12'  # preserves the pin actions/setup-python held
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"

      - name: Install JMo Security and test dependencies
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions == 'true'
        run: uv sync --locked --group dev

      - name: Put the project venv on PATH
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -d .venv/Scripts ]; then
            cygpath -w "$PWD/.venv/Scripts" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          else
            echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          fi

      - name: Install security tools for contract tests
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions == 'true'
        env:
          # Pinned to versions.yaml. Update both files together when bumping.
          TRIVY_VERSION: "0.74.0"
          TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION: "3.97.1"
          HADOLINT_VERSION: "2.15.1"
        run: |
          # Same install block as scheduled.yml:tool-contract-tests — kept in
          # sync manually. Any drift means the weekly and PR gates disagree.
          # All downloads pinned + hardened (--fail + retry + integrity)
          # to avoid the upstream install.sh GitHub API flake. See PR #350
          # and release.rules.md "CI install hardening".
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 600 \
            "https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/download/v${TRIVY_VERSION}/trivy_${TRIVY_VERSION}_Linux-64bit.tar.gz" \
            -o /tmp/trivy.tar.gz
          gzip -t /tmp/trivy.tar.gz
          tar -xzf /tmp/trivy.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin trivy
          pip install semgrep bandit checkov
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 600 \
            "https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint/releases/download/v${HADOLINT_VERSION}/hadolint-Linux-x86_64" \
            -o /usr/local/bin/hadolint
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/hadolint
          v="$TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION"  # short alias to keep URL line under 140 chars
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 600 \
            "https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/releases/download/v${v}/trufflehog_${v}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
            -o /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz
          gzip -t /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz
          tar -xzf /tmp/trufflehog.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin trufflehog
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/trufflehog
          sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck

          echo "Installed tools:"
          trivy --version || echo "trivy not available"
          semgrep --version || echo "semgrep not available"
          bandit --version || echo "bandit not available"
          hadolint --version || echo "hadolint not available"
          trufflehog --version || echo "trufflehog not available"
          checkov --version || echo "checkov not available"
          shellcheck --version || echo "shellcheck not available"

      - name: Run tool contract tests
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions == 'true'
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: |
          pytest tests/integration/test_tool_contracts.py \
            -v \
            -m "requires_tools" \
            --tb=short \
            --timeout=300

      - name: Summarize skip
        if: steps.changes.outputs.versions != 'true'
        run: |
          echo "No version-affecting files changed — contract tests not required."
          echo "Paths watched: versions.yaml, Dockerfile.*, tests/integration/test_tool_contracts.py"

  # ==========================================================================
  # phase-audit -- is every open issue scheduled, and do the labels agree?
  # ==========================================================================
  # The bar this replaces was "re-run the unclaimed-issue query at the start of
  # each remaining phase". That is a habit, and it decayed silently three times
  # in a row -- chunk 22's sweep was true when it closed, and every issue filed
  # afterwards went unexamined. Each check since has been a hand-maintained
  # list, including the one at Phase 2 closeout, which omitted an issue.
  #
  # The plan's phase rosters are the single source; `phase:N` labels are
  # derived from them. `verify` fails on an open issue the plan names nowhere,
  # and on any roster/label disagreement in EITHER direction.
  #
  # pull_request only, not push: every branch push runs this workflow twice and
  # the two see different worlds, so gating on both just doubles the noise.
  phase-audit:
    name: phase-audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # Fork PRs are skipped, not passed. A contributor's PR cannot be
    # responsible for repo-wide issue scheduling, and a skipped job reads
    # differently from a green one -- which is the property that matters.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
       github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      # No `uv sync`: phase_audit.py is stdlib-only by design, so this job
      # cannot be broken by a dependency change it has nothing to do with.
      - name: Verify the plan parses and its own checksums agree
        run: python scripts/dev/phase_audit.py derive

      - name: Verify every open issue is scheduled and the labels match
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: python scripts/dev/phase_audit.py verify
